titre: The Most Closely Studied Body in the World, Read Twice Over
accroche: Ötzi yielded an arrow ten years after his discovery, and a genome that had to be rewritten eleven years after that
contenu_vulgarise:
In September 1991, two hikers find a body emerging from the ice, at more than three thousand meters in the Ötztal Alps. At first it is taken for a recent mountain accident. The body is about 5,300 years old.

Preservation by cold kept what no site usually yields: the skin, the tattoos, the stomach contents, the clothing, an unfinished bow, a copper-bladed ax.

This body has become the most examined archaeological object in the world. Its story is also the story of two revisions.

## The arrow no one had seen

For ten years, researchers look for why he died. Exhaustion, cold, a fall: hypotheses follow one another over a body that is nonetheless scrutinized.

In 2001, an X-ray reveals a flint arrowhead lodged in the left shoulder. The entry wound in the back, two centimeters wide, which had gone unnoticed, is then identified.

The arrow severed a subclavian artery. The cause of death is no longer bad weather. It is hemorrhage, and the shot came from behind.

Ten years of examinations had not been enough. You only find what you look for with the right instrument.

## The genome that had to be rewritten

In 2012, a team publishes Ötzi's genome, one of the first ancient genomes ever sequenced. The portrait that emerges circulates at once: light skin, brown eyes, and a share of ancestry from the Eurasian steppes.

In 2023, a reanalysis of the same material with finer techniques corrects almost everything.

The 2012 sample was largely contaminated with modern DNA, that of the people who had handled the body. The steppe ancestry disappears entirely from the new picture: it was the artifact. Ötzi instead shows an unusually high proportion of Anatolian farmer ancestry, higher than in any known European population of his time.

And the portrait changes with it: dark skin, advanced male-pattern baldness.

## What this double revision teaches

A body this complete gives the illusion of a direct reading. We think we are consulting a document rather than interpreting traces.

The two corrections say the opposite. The first came down to the instrument: without the X-ray, the arrow did not exist. The second came down to contamination: an ancient genome is always mixed with the genomes of those who touched it, and telling the two apart depends on a technique that keeps improving.

Ötzi has not changed. It is our means of reading him that have changed twice, and nothing says the current reading is the last.

repere.texte: The 2023 reanalysis makes the steppe ancestry attributed to Ötzi in 2012 disappear: it was contamination by modern DNA. His share of Anatolian ancestry is the highest known for Europe in his time.
repere.source: Wang, Prüfer et al., “High-coverage genome of the Tyrolean Iceman reveals unusually high Anatolian farmer ancestry,” Cell Genomics, 2023

carte.punch: Ötzi hasn't changed. Our means of reading him have changed twice.
carte.idee: The arrow that killed him was not seen until 2001, ten years after the discovery. And his 2012 genome, contaminated with modern DNA, had to be rewritten in 2023: neither light skin nor steppe ancestry.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Nature — Ötzi the Iceman has a new look: balding and dark-skinned
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: In English, short; explains the 2012 contamination in a few paragraphs.

quiz.question: Why did Ötzi's genome, published in 2012, have to be corrected?
choix: Because the samples taken came from another body at the same site
Because it was largely mixed with the DNA of the people who had handled the body
Because the dating of the body had been revised by several centuries in the meantime
Because the tattoos had been interpreted as marks of disease
quiz.explication: Contamination by modern DNA is the central problem of ancient genomes: it had created from scratch the steppe ancestry attributed to Ötzi. The 2023 techniques make it possible to tell it apart, which made this signal disappear and changed the physical portrait. Neither the identity of the body nor its dating was called into question.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Under what circumstances is Ötzi's body discovered in 1991, and what is it first mistaken for?
choix: A team of cavers finds a body in an underground cave, never exposed to the cold
Archaeologists on a planned dig unearth a body deliberately buried under a cairn
Two hikers find a body emerging from the ice at more than three thousand meters, at first taken for a recent accident
A shepherd finds a body at the bottom of an Alpine lake dried up by an exceptional drought
quiz_supplementaire.explication: In September 1991, two hikers find a body emerging from the ice at more than three thousand meters in the Ötztal Alps; at first it is taken for a recent mountain accident, before it turns out to be about 5,300 years old.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What exactly does the 2001 X-ray reveal about the cause of Ötzi's death?
choix: A skull fracture caused by a block of ice falling in an avalanche
Poisoning by toxic berries found in his stomach contents
A wild animal bite on the right leg, leading to a fatal infection
A flint arrowhead lodged in the left shoulder, which severed a subclavian artery, shot from behind
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 2001 X-ray reveals a flint arrowhead lodged in the left shoulder, matching an entry wound in the back that went unnoticed for ten years: the arrow severed a subclavian artery, causing death by hemorrhage, shot from behind.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What concretely does the 2023 genomic reanalysis change about the portrait and ancestry of Ötzi established in 2012?
choix: Dark skin and advanced baldness replace the 2012 portrait, and the steppe ancestry disappears
The 2012 portrait is fully confirmed, and only the dating of the body is slightly revised
North African ancestry replaces the steppe ancestry initially identified in 2012
Eye color changes from blue to green, with no change to ancestry or pigmentation
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 2023 reanalysis makes the 2012 steppe ancestry disappear, an artifact of contamination by modern DNA, in favor of an unusually high Anatolian farmer ancestry, and changes the physical portrait: dark skin, advanced male-pattern baldness.
